page_title: Graphlit — Context layer for AI agents

summary.name: Graphlit
summary.one_liner: Graphlit is a context layer API that ingests content from tools like Slack, GitHub, and Jira and models entities, relationships, and temporal state so AI agents can retrieve grounded, source-cited context.
use_cases: sync Slack, GitHub, and Jira data into an agent knowledge base
replace glue code between RAG pipelines and vector stores
ground chatbot answers with cited sources
track entities and how they change over time
connect Claude Desktop or Cursor to company data via MCP
summary.what_it_does: Graphlit provides a single API that handles content ingestion, extraction, enrichment, storage, and retrieval for AI agents. It ingests documents, PDFs, audio, video, web pages, and messages from sources such as Slack, email, Jira, RSS, Web, and Notion, and applies transcription, OCR, and object detection. It extracts entities, relationships, ownership, events, and temporal state, and uses LLM-based entity resolution. Search is available by text or vector similarity, and a chatbot feature supports RAG with cited sources. The page says SDKs exist for Python, Node.js, and .NET, and it offers an MCP server installable via npx.
notable: Entity and relationship modeling with LLM-based entity resolution and temporal state
Continuous real-time sync from sources like Slack, GitHub, and Jira
MCP server installable via npx for Cursor, VS Code, and Claude Desktop
Full provenance linking answers back to source content
caveats: Free tier is limited usage; further use is usage-based credits
Page mentions existing customers can continue to sign in and manage usage, suggesting a changed or legacy pricing arrangement
Content cost estimates are averages and actual costs vary
